title: त्रयोविंशतितमोऽध्यायः
titleEn: Adhyaya 23 · Arjuna and Krishna against Shakuni's horse

summary.en: The Kaurava riders, hearing the Pandavas' roar, gather again around Shakuni and Uluka, and Arjuna goes against them at Krishna's word. Arjuna, with the Gandiva, cuts through the masses of horsemen.
summary.kn: ಪಾಂಡವರ ಗರ್ಜನೆ ಕೇಳಿ ಕೌರವ ಸವಾರರು ಶಕುನಿ, ಉಲೂಕರ ಸುತ್ತ ಮತ್ತೆ ಸೇರುತ್ತಾರೆ; ಕೃಷ್ಣನ ಮಾತಿನಂತೆ ಅರ್ಜುನ ಅವರ ಮೇಲೆ ಹೋಗುತ್ತಾನೆ. ಗಾಂಡೀವದಿಂದ ಅರ್ಜುನ ಅಶ್ವಾರೋಹಿ ಸಮೂಹಗಳನ್ನು ಸೀಳುತ್ತಾನೆ.
summary.hi: पाण्डवों की गर्जना सुनकर कौरव घुड़सवार शकुनि और उलूक के चारों ओर फिर जुटते हैं, और अर्जुन कृष्ण के कहने पर उन पर जाते हैं। अर्जुन गाण्डीव से घुड़सवारों के समूहों को चीर देते हैं।
summary.te: పాండవుల గర్జన విని కౌరవ అశ్వికులు శకుని, ఉలూకుల చుట్టూ మళ్లీ చేరతారు; కృష్ణుని మాట మేరకు అర్జునుడు వారిపైకి వెళతాడు. గాండీవంతో అర్జునుడు అశ్వికుల సమూహాలను చీల్చుతాడు.
summary.ta: பாண்டவரின் முழக்கம் கேட்ட கௌரவக் குதிரை வீரர் சகுனி, உலூகனைச் சுற்றித் திரள, கண்ணனின் சொற்படி அர்ஜுனன் அவர்களை நோக்கிச் செல்கிறான். காண்டீவத்தால் அர்ஜுனன் குதிரைப்படைத் திரள்களைப் பிளக்கிறான்.
summary.ml: പാണ്ഡവരുടെ ഗർജ്ജനം കേട്ട കൗരവ അശ്വാരോഹികൾ, ശകുനിയെയും ഉലൂകനെയും ചുറ്റി വീണ്ടും ഒന്നിച്ചുകൂടുന്നു; കൃഷ്ണന്റെ വാക്കിൽ അർജുനൻ അവർക്കെതിരെ നീങ്ങുന്നു. ഗാണ്ഡീവം കൈയിലെടുത്ത അർജുനൻ, കുതിരപ്പട്ടാളത്തിന്റെ കൂട്ടങ്ങളെ വെട്ടിമുറിക്കുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 9.23; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Tue Jun 23 2020

verses.text: संजय उवाच

meaning.en: Sanjaya said:

verses.text:
तस्मिञ्शब्दे मृदौ जाते पाण्डवैर्निहते बले ।
अश्वैः सप्तशतैः शिष्टैरुपावर्तत सौबलः ॥

meaning.en: When that clamor had softened and the force had been struck down by the Pandavas, Shakuni, son of Subala, turned back with seven hundred horses that remained.

verses.text:
स यात्वा वाहिनीं तूर्णमब्रवीत्त्वरयन्युधि ।
युध्यध्वमिति संहृष्टाः पुनः पुनररिंदमः ।
अपृच्छत्क्षत्रियांस्तत्र क्व नु राजा महारथः ॥

meaning.en: Having quickly reached the army, that tamer of foes urged them on in the battle, cheering them again and again: "Fight!" And he asked the kshatriyas there, "Where is the king, the great chariot-fighter?"

verses.text:
शकुनेस्तु वचः श्रुत्वा त ऊचुर्भरतर्षभ ।
असौ तिष्ठति कौरव्यो रणमध्ये महारथः ॥

meaning.en: Hearing Shakuni's words, O bull of the Bharatas, they said: "That Kuru, the great chariot-fighter, stands in the middle of the battle,

verses.text:
यत्रैतत्सुमहच्छत्रं पूर्णचन्द्रसमप्रभम् ।
यत्रैते सतलत्राणा रथास्तिष्ठन्ति दंशिताः ॥

meaning.en: where that very large white parasol shines like the full moon, where those armored chariots stand with their guards,

verses.text:
यत्रैष शब्दस्तुमुलः पर्जन्यनिनदोपमः ।
तत्र गच्छ द्रुतं राजंस्ततो द्रक्ष्यसि कौरवम् ॥

meaning.en: and where that tumultuous noise like the roar of a rain cloud rises. Go there quickly, O king, and you will see the Kaurava."

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तु तैः शूरैः शकुनिः सौबलस्तदा ।
प्रययौ तत्र यत्रासौ पुत्रस्तव नराधिप ।
सर्वतः संवृतो वीरैः समरेष्वनिवर्तिभिः ॥

meaning.en: Told this by those heroes, Shakuni, son of Subala, went to where your son was, O king, surrounded on all sides by heroes who never retreat from battle.

verses.text:
ततो दुर्योधनं दृष्ट्वा रथानीके व्यवस्थितम् ।
सरथांस्तावकान्सर्वान्हर्षयञ्शकुनिस्ततः ॥

meaning.en: Then seeing Duryodhana stationed in the chariot force, Shakuni cheered all your men with their chariots.

verses.text:
दुर्योधनमिदं वाक्यं हृष्टरूपो विशां पते ।
कृतकार्यमिवात्मानं मन्यमानोऽब्रवीन्नृपम् ॥

meaning.en: Joyful, O lord of the people, and thinking his work already done, he spoke these words to King Duryodhana:

verses.text:
जहि राजन्रथानीकमश्वाः सर्वे जिता मया ।
नात्यक्त्वा जीवितं संख्ये शक्यो जेतुं युधिष्ठिरः ॥

meaning.en: "Strike the chariot force, O king; I have beaten all their horses. Yudhishthira cannot be conquered in battle without giving up one's life.

verses.text:
हते तस्मिन्रथानीके पाण्डवेनाभिपालिते ।
गजानेतान्हनिष्यामः पदातींश्चेतरांस्तथा ॥

meaning.en: When that chariot force, guarded by the Pandava, is destroyed, we shall kill these elephants and the foot soldiers and the rest."

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तस्य तावका जयगृद्धिनः ।
जवेनाभ्यपतन्हृष्टाः पाण्डवानामनीकिनीम् ॥

meaning.en: Hearing his words, your men, eager for victory, rushed gladly and fast at the Pandava army.

verses.text:
सर्वे विवृततूणीराः प्रगृहीतशरासनाः ।
शरासनानि धुन्वानाः सिंहनादं प्रचक्रिरे ॥

meaning.en: All of them, with quivers opened and bows in hand, shook their bows and gave lion-roars.

verses.text:
ततो ज्यातलनिर्घोषः पुनरासीद्विशां पते ।
प्रादुरासीच्छराणां च सुमुक्तानां सुदारुणः ॥

meaning.en: Then again, O lord of the people, there was the sound of bowstrings slapping the palm and the terrible whirr of arrows well loosed.

verses.text:
तान्समीपगतान्दृष्ट्वा जवेनोद्यतकार्मुकान् ।
उवाच देवकीपुत्रं कुन्तीपुत्रो धनंजयः ॥

meaning.en: Seeing them come close, bows raised, at speed, Dhananjaya, Kunti's son, said to Devaki's son:

verses.text:
चोदयाश्वानसंभ्रान्तः प्रविशैतद्बलार्णवम् ।
अन्तमद्य गमिष्यामि शत्रूणां निशितैः शरैः ॥

meaning.en: "Drive the horses on without confusion and enter this ocean of troops. Today with my sharp arrows I will bring the enemy to an end.

verses.text:
अष्टादश दिनान्यद्य युद्धस्यास्य जनार्दन ।
वर्तमानस्य महतः समासाद्य परस्परम् ॥

meaning.en: Today, Janardana, is the eighteenth day of this great battle that has gone on as they have met one another.

verses.text:
अनन्तकल्पा ध्वजिनी भूत्वा ह्येषां महात्मनाम् ।
क्षयमद्य गता युद्धे पश्य दैवं यथाविधम् ॥

meaning.en: Their army, which was once endless in extent, has been brought to destruction in battle today, along with those great men. See how fate works!

verses.text:
समुद्रकल्पं तु बलं धार्तराष्ट्रस्य माधव ।
अस्मानासाद्य संजातं गोष्पदोपममच्युत ॥

meaning.en: The Dhartarashtra's force, Madhava, was like an ocean; having met us, it has become like a cow's hoofprint, O Achyuta.

verses.text:
हते भीष्मे च संदध्याच्छिवं स्यादिह माधव ।
न च तत्कृतवान्मूढो धार्तराष्ट्रः सुबालिशः ॥

meaning.en: When Bhishma was slain, he could have made peace, and good would have come of it here, O Madhava. But the foolish and childish Dhartarashtra did not do so.

verses.text:
उक्तं भीष्मेण यद्वाक्यं हितं पथ्यं च माधव ।
तच्चापि नासौ कृतवान्वीतबुद्धिः सुयोधनः ॥

meaning.en: Even the beneficial, wholesome words that Bhishma spoke, O Madhava, the senseless Suyodhana did not act on.

verses.text:
तस्मिंस्तु पतिते भीष्मे प्रच्युते पृथिवीतले ।
न जाने कारणं किं नु येन युद्धमवर्तत ॥

meaning.en: When Bhishma fell and dropped to the surface of the earth, I do not know what reason made the battle go on.

verses.text:
मूढांस्तु सर्वथा मन्ये धार्तराष्ट्रान्सुबालिशान् ।
पतिते शंतनोः पुत्रे येऽकार्षुः संयुगं पुनः ॥

meaning.en: I think the Dhartarashtras are utterly foolish and childish, who made war again when Shantanu's son had fallen.

verses.text:
अनन्तरं च निहते द्रोणे ब्रह्मविदां वरे ।
राधेये च विकर्णे च नैवाशाम्यत वैशसम् ॥

meaning.en: And then, when Drona, best of the knowers of Brahman, was killed, and Radheya and Vikarna as well, the slaughter still did not stop.

verses.text:
अल्पावशिष्टे सैन्येऽस्मिन्सूतपुत्रे च पातिते ।
सपुत्रे वै नरव्याघ्रे नैवाशाम्यत वैशसम् ॥

meaning.en: When this army was reduced to a remnant, and the charioteer's son, that tiger among men, was felled together with his sons, the slaughter still did not stop.

verses.text:
श्रुतायुषि हते शूरे जलसंधे च पौरवे ।
श्रुतायुधे च नृपतौ नैवाशाम्यत वैशसम् ॥

meaning.en: When the brave Shrutayus was slain, and Jalasandha, and the Paurava, and King Shrutayudha, the slaughter still did not stop.

verses.text:
भूरिश्रवसि शल्ये च शाल्वे चैव जनार्दन ।
आवन्त्येषु च वीरेषु नैवाशाम्यत वैशसम् ॥

meaning.en: When Bhurishravas, Shalya and Shalva had fallen, O Janardana, and the heroes of Avanti, the slaughter still did not stop.

verses.text:
जयद्रथे च निहते राक्षसे चाप्यलायुधे ।
बाह्लिके सोमदत्ते च नैवाशाम्यत वैशसम् ॥

meaning.en: When Jayadratha was killed, and the rakshasa Alayudha, and Bahlika and Somadatta, the slaughter still did not stop.

verses.text:
भगदत्ते हते शूरे काम्बोजे च सुदक्षिणे ।
दुःशासने च निहते नैवाशाम्यत वैशसम् ॥

meaning.en: When the brave Bhagadatta was killed, and Sudakshina of the Kambojas, and Duhshasana, the slaughter still did not stop.

verses.text:
दृष्ट्वा च निहताञ्शूरान्पृथङ्माण्डलिकान्नृपान् ।
बलिनश्च रणे कृष्ण नैवाशाम्यत वैशसम् ॥

meaning.en: Even after seeing the brave and mighty petty kings killed in the battle, one by one, O Krishna, the slaughter did not stop.

verses.text:
अक्षौहिणीपतीन्दृष्ट्वा भीमसेनेन पातितान् ।
मोहाद्वा यदि वा लोभान्नैवाशाम्यत वैशसम् ॥

meaning.en: Seeing the lords of akshauhinis felled by Bhimasena, whether from delusion or greed, he still did not stop the slaughter.

verses.text:
को नु राजकुले जातः कौरवेयो विशेषतः ।
निरर्थकं महद्वैरं कुर्यादन्यः सुयोधनात् ॥

meaning.en: Who born in a royal house, and a Kaurava especially, other than Suyodhana, would carry on a great enmity with no purpose?

verses.text:
गुणतोऽभ्यधिकं ज्ञात्वा बलतः शौर्यतोऽपि वा ।
अमूढः को नु युध्येत जानन्प्राज्ञो हिताहितम् ॥

meaning.en: Knowing the other side to be better in quality, in strength and in valor, what undeluded, wise man who knows his good from his harm would fight?

verses.text:
यन्न तस्य मनो ह्यासीत्त्वयोक्तस्य हितं वचः ।
प्रशमे पाण्डवैः सार्धं सोऽन्यस्य शृणुयात्कथम् ॥

meaning.en: He whose mind was not turned to peace with the Pandavas even by your beneficial words, how would he listen to anyone else?

verses.text:
येन शांतनवो भीष्मो द्रोणो विदुर एव च ।
प्रत्याख्याताः शमस्यार्थे किं नु तस्याद्य भेषजम् ॥

meaning.en: He who rejected Bhishma son of Shantanu, Drona and Vidura too when they spoke for peace: what medicine is there for him now?

verses.text:
मौर्ख्याद्येन पिता वृद्धः प्रत्याख्यातो जनार्दन ।
तथा माता हितं वाक्यं भाषमाणा हितैषिणी ।
प्रत्याख्याता ह्यसत्कृत्य स कस्मै रोचयेद्वचः ॥

meaning.en: He who in his folly rejected his aged father, O Janardana, and likewise his well-wishing mother who spoke beneficial words, treating them with disrespect: to whom would he ever listen?

verses.text:
कुलान्तकरणो व्यक्तं जात एष जनार्दन ।
तथास्य दृश्यते चेष्टा नीतिश्चैव विशां पते ।
नैष दास्यति नो राज्यमिति मे मतिरच्युत ॥

meaning.en: He has plainly been born to end his family, O Janardana. His conduct and policy show it, O lord of the people. I believe, Achyuta, that he will never give us the kingdom.

verses.text:
उक्तोऽहं बहुशस्तात विदुरेण महात्मना ।
न जीवन्दास्यते भागं धार्तराष्ट्रः कथंचन ॥

meaning.en: Many times the great-souled Vidura said to me, "Dear child, the Dhartarashtra will never give your share while he lives.

verses.text:
यावत्प्राणा धमिष्यन्ति धार्तराष्ट्रस्य मानद ।
तावद्युष्मास्वपापेषु प्रचरिष्यति पातकम् ॥

meaning.en: As long as breath keeps moving in the Dhartarashtra, O giver of honor, he will go on committing wrong against you innocent men.

verses.text:
न स युक्तोऽन्यथा जेतुमृते युद्धेन माधव ।
इत्यब्रवीत्सदा मां हि विदुरः सत्यदर्शनः ॥

meaning.en: He cannot be conquered in any other way, Madhava, except by war." So Vidura, who sees the truth, always told me.

verses.text:
तत्सर्वमद्य जानामि व्यवसायं दुरात्मनः ।
यदुक्तं वचनं तेन विदुरेण महात्मना ॥

meaning.en: Today I understand all of it, the resolve of that wicked man, in the words that the great-souled Vidura spoke.

verses.text:
यो हि श्रुत्वा वचः पथ्यं जामदग्न्याद्यथातथम् ।
अवामन्यत दुर्बुद्धिर्ध्रुवं नाशमुखे स्थितः ॥

meaning.en: One who, hearing the true and wholesome words of Jamadagni's son, scorned them, that fool surely stands at the mouth of ruin.

verses.text:
उक्तं हि बहुभिः सिद्धैर्जातमात्रे सुयोधने ।
एनं प्राप्य दुरात्मानं क्षयं क्षत्रं गमिष्यति ॥

meaning.en: Many Siddhas said when Suyodhana was just born: "Reaching this wicked man, the warrior class will go to destruction."

verses.text:
तदिदं वचनं तेषां निरुक्तं वै जनार्दन ।
क्षयं याता हि राजानो दुर्योधनकृते भृशम् ॥

meaning.en: That prophecy of theirs, Janardana, has been fulfilled: the kings have gone to utter ruin for Duryodhana's sake.

verses.text:
सोऽद्य सर्वान्रणे योधान्निहनिष्यामि माधव ।
क्षत्रियेषु हतेष्वाशु शून्ये च शिबिरे कृते ॥

meaning.en: Today, Madhava, I will kill all the warriors in the battle; when the kshatriyas are quickly slain and the camp left empty,

verses.text:
वधाय चात्मनोऽस्माभिः संयुगं रोचयिष्यति ।
तदन्तं हि भवेद्वैरमनुमानेन माधव ॥

meaning.en: he will choose to fight us to bring about his own death. Then, Madhava, this enmity will end, as I reckon it.

verses.text:
एवं पश्यामि वार्ष्णेय चिन्तयन्प्रज्ञया स्वया ।
विदुरस्य च वाक्येन चेष्टया च दुरात्मनः ॥

meaning.en: So I see it, Vrishni, reflecting with my own judgment, from Vidura's words and the wicked man's conduct.

verses.text:
संयाहि भारतीं वीर यावद्धन्मि शितैः शरैः ।
दुर्योधनं दुरात्मानं वाहिनीं चास्य संयुगे ॥

meaning.en: Drive on, hero, into the Kuru force, while I strike down the wicked Duryodhana and his army in battle with sharp arrows.

verses.text:
क्षेममद्य करिष्यामि धर्मराजस्य माधव ।
हत्वैतद्दुर्बलं सैन्यं धार्तराष्ट्रस्य पश्यतः ॥

meaning.en: Today I will bring safety to the king of dharma, Madhava, by destroying, before the Dhartarashtra's eyes, this weakened army of his."

verses.text: संजय उवाच

meaning.en: Sanjaya said:

verses.text:
अभीशुहस्तो दाशार्हस्तथोक्तः सव्यसाचिना ।
तद्बलौघममित्राणामभीतः प्राविशद्रणे ॥

meaning.en: Thus addressed by Savyasachin, the Dasharha, reins in hand, fearlessly drove into that flood of enemy troops in the battle.

verses.text:
शरासनवरं घोरं शक्तिकण्टकसंवृतम् ।
गदापरिघपन्थानं रथनागमहाद्रुमम् ॥

meaning.en: The renowned Govinda roamed there in his chariot with its many banners, plunging into that fearsome sea whose finest bow-shapes were its waves, thick with spears for thorns, with maces and clubs for paths and chariots and elephants for great trees,

verses.text:
हयपत्तिलताकीर्णं गाहमानो महायशाः ।
व्यचरत्तत्र गोविन्दो रथेनातिपताकिना ॥

meaning.en: strewn with horses and foot soldiers as vines.

verses.text:
ते हयाः पाण्डुरा राजन्वहन्तोऽर्जुनमाहवे ।
दिक्षु सर्वास्वदृश्यन्त दाशार्हेण प्रचोदिताः ॥

meaning.en: Those white horses, O king, carrying Arjuna in the battle and driven by the Dasharha, were seen in every direction.

verses.text:
ततः प्रायाद्रथेनाजौ सव्यसाची परंतपः ।
किरञ्शरशतांस्तीक्ष्णान्वारिधारा इवाम्बुदः ॥

meaning.en: Then Savyasachin, scorcher of foes, went on in his chariot in the battle, scattering hundreds of sharp arrows as a cloud pours streams of water.

verses.text:
प्रादुरासीन्महाञ्शब्दः शराणां नतपर्वणाम् ।
इषुभिश्छाद्यमानानां समरे सव्यसाचिना ॥

meaning.en: A great noise arose from the straight-jointed arrows as they covered the enemy in the battle, shot by Savyasachin.

verses.text:
असज्जन्तस्तनुत्रेषु शरौघाः प्रापतन्भुवि ।
इन्द्राशनिसमस्पर्शा गाण्डीवप्रेषिताः शराः ॥

meaning.en: Floods of arrows, shot from the Gandiva with a touch like Indra's thunderbolt, did not stick in armor but fell to the ground.

verses.text:
नरान्नागान्समाहत्य हयांश्चापि विशां पते ।
अपतन्त रणे बाणाः पतंगा इव घोषिणः ॥

meaning.en: Striking men, elephants and horses, O lord of the people, the arrows fell in the battle like humming locusts.

verses.text:
आसीत्सर्वमवच्छन्नं गाण्डीवप्रेषितैः शरैः ।
न प्राज्ञायन्त समरे दिशो वा प्रदिशोऽपि वा ॥

meaning.en: Everything was veiled by the arrows loosed from the Gandiva, and in the battle neither the directions nor the intermediate directions could be made out.

verses.text:
सर्वमासीज्जगत्पूर्णं पार्थनामाङ्कितैः शरैः ।
रुक्मपुङ्खैस्तैलधौतैः कर्मारपरिमार्जितैः ॥

meaning.en: The whole world was filled with arrows marked with Partha's name, gold-feathered, oil-washed and polished by the smith.

verses.text:
ते दह्यमानाः पार्थेन पावकेनेव कुञ्जराः ।
समासीदन्त कौरव्या वध्यमानाः शितैः शरैः ॥

meaning.en: Scorched by Partha as elephants are by fire, the Kauravas pressed together, struck down by sharp arrows.

verses.text:
शरचापधरः पार्थः प्रज्वलन्निव भारत ।
ददाह समरे योधान्कक्षमग्निरिव ज्वलन् ॥

meaning.en: Partha, bearing arrows and bow, blazed as it were, O Bharata, and burned the warriors in the battle as a blazing fire burns dry grass.

verses.text:
यथा वनान्ते वनपैर्विसृष्टः
कक्षं दहेत्कृष्णगतिः सघोषः ।
भूरिद्रुमं शुष्कलतावितानं
भृशं समृद्धो ज्वलनः प्रतापी ॥

meaning.en: As, at the edge of a forest, a fire let loose by foresters, black-pathed and roaring, burns dry grass and many trees entwined with dry creepers, and grows greatly, mighty,

verses.text:
एवं स नाराचगणप्रतापी
शरार्चिरुच्चावचतिग्मतेजाः ।
ददाह सर्वां तव पुत्रसेना-
ममृष्यमाणस्तरसा तरस्वी ॥

meaning.en: so he, mighty with showers of iron arrows, his arrows the flames, of varied and fierce blaze, burned all your son's army swiftly, in his impatience.

verses.text:
तस्येषवः प्राणहराः सुमुक्ता
नासज्जन्वै वर्मसु रुक्मपुङ्खाः ।
न च द्वितीयं प्रमुमोच बाणं
नरे हये वा परमद्विपे वा ॥

meaning.en: His life-taking, gold-feathered arrows, well loosed, did not stick in armor; and he never shot a second arrow at any man, horse or great elephant.

verses.text:
अनेकरूपाकृतिभिर्हि बाणै-
र्महारथानीकमनुप्रविश्य ।
स एव एकस्तव पुत्रसेनां
जघान दैत्यानिव वज्रपाणिः ॥

meaning.en: Entering the great chariot force with arrows of many shapes and forms, he alone slew your son's army, as the thunderbolt-wielder slew the Daityas.
